statement: For any natural number n, including 0, let I=Fin n={0,...,n-1}. RealMatrix n is R^(I×I), and Vector n is R^I. All vector operations are coordinatewise; (Mv)_i=sum over j in I of M_ij v_j. Matrix products and natural powers are ordinary matrix operations, with M^0 the identity. Write |v| and |M| for entrywise absolute values, ||v||∞=max({0}∪{|v_i|:i in I}), and ||M||∞=max({0}∪{sum over j in I of |M_ij|:i in I}); both are 0 for n=0. The total matrix inverse D^(-1) is the ordinary inverse when det D≠0 and the zero matrix when det D=0. Let T=-D^(-1)N, c(y)=D^(-1)(b-Ay), U(y)=y+c(y), y_0=x₀, y_(k+1)=U(y_k), c_k=c(y_k), and e_k=y_k-x. The function rho(M) takes the extended nonnegative complex spectral radius of the entrywise complexification of M and converts it to a real number using ENNReal.toReal, which sends infinity to 0. For these finite matrices this is the largest modulus of a complex eigenvalue, with value 0 for an empty spectrum. The sole target concerns this residual-correction iteration, under the splitting and solution hypotheses below, and asserts error identities, quantitative bounds, a convergence equivalence, and a sufficient contraction condition.

targets.name: Research.BlockJacobi.block_jacobi_real
targets.statement: For every natural number n≥0, arbitrary type/set B (at any universe level), function block:I→B, real matrices A,D,N in R^(I×I), and real vectors b,x in R^I, assume A=D+N; for all i,j in I, block(i)≠block(j) implies D_ij=0; for all i,j in I, block(i)=block(j) implies N_ij=0; det D is a unit in R (equivalently det D≠0); and Ax=b. Using exactly the constructions and notation in the summary, the following conjunction holds. (1) For every x₀ in R^I and integer k≥0, D c_k=b-Ay_k, y_(k+1)=y_k+c_k, e_(k+1)=T e_k, e_k=T^k e_0, for every i in I one has |(e_k)_i|≤((|T|)^k |e_0|)_i, and ||e_k||∞≤(||T||∞)^k ||e_0||∞. (2) rho(T)=rho(D^(-1)N). (3) The assertion that for every x₀ in R^I the sequence k↦y_k tends to x as k→∞ through the natural numbers is equivalent to rho(T)<1. Convergence is in the usual product topology on R^I, equivalently coordinatewise convergence. (4) If ||T||∞<1, then for every x₀ in R^I this convergence holds, 0≤||T||∞, and for every u,v in R^I one has ||U(u)-U(v)||∞≤||T||∞ ||u-v||∞. Here the actual update is U(y)=y+D^(-1)(b-Ay); under the hypotheses it also equals D^(-1)b+Ty. The given x is a fixed specified solution throughout all these conclusions. No positive-dimension restriction or injectivity/surjectivity condition on block is assumed.

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.IsBlockDecomposition
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0 and arbitrary type/set B, takes block:I→B and A,D,N in R^(I×I). It asserts exactly A=D+N, and, for all i,j in I, D_ij=0 if block(i)≠block(j), while N_ij=0 if block(i)=block(j). Consequently D retains the within-label entries of A and N retains the between-label entries. It asserts no invertibility or condition on the labels.

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.vectorInfNorm
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0 and v in R^I, returns max({0}∪{|v_i|:i in I}) as a real number: the finite supremum of the nonnegative real norms of all coordinates, coerced to R. It is 0 for an empty index set.

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.matrixInfNorm
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0 and M in R^(I×I), returns max({0}∪{sum over j in I of |M_ij|:i in I}) as a real number. It sums nonnegative real entry norms in each row, takes their finite supremum, and coerces to R. It is 0 if n=0.

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.vectorAbs
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0 and v in R^I, returns the vector i↦|v_i| for every i in I.

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.matrixAbs
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0 and M in R^(I×I), returns the entrywise absolute-value matrix (i,j)↦|M_ij| for every i,j in I.

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.complexification
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0 and M in R^(I×I), returns the matrix in C^(I×I) whose entries are the images of M_ij under the canonical embedding R→C, that is M_ij+0i.

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.rho
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0 and M in R^(I×I), returns ENNReal.toReal(spectralRadius over C of complexification(M)). The extended nonnegative spectral radius is the supremum of the moduli of the complex spectrum; the real conversion preserves finite values and sends infinity to 0. For a finite matrix this is the maximum modulus of its complex eigenvalues, with empty-spectrum value 0. It uses the complexified matrix, so the spectrum is not restricted to real eigenvalues.

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.iterationMatrix
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0 and D,N in R^(I×I), returns -(D^(-1)N), using the total inverse convention in the summary. The definition requires neither nonsingularity nor a block decomposition.

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.correctionAt
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0, A,D in R^(I×I), and b,y in R^I, returns D^(-1)(b-Ay). It applies the inverse of the entire matrix D to the residual, with no block-label parameter or hypotheses.

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.update
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0, A,D in R^(I×I), and b,y in R^I, returns y+correctionAt(A,D,b,y)=y+D^(-1)(b-Ay). Under the theorem hypotheses it is D^(-1)b-D^(-1)Ny. Its definition has no hypotheses.

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.iterate
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0, A,D in R^(I×I), b,x₀ in R^I, and natural number k≥0, returns y_k from the recursion y_0=x₀ and y_(k+1)=update(A,D,b,y_k)=y_k+D^(-1)(b-Ay_k). The recursion repeatedly performs the residual update for fixed A,D,b. It does not take N or block as an argument and has no hypotheses.

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.correction
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0, A,D in R^(I×I), b,x₀ in R^I, and natural number k≥0, returns correctionAt(A,D,b,iterate(A,D,b,x₀,k))=D^(-1)(b-Ay_k). This is the correction added in the transition from y_k to y_(k+1).

constructions.name: Research.BlockJacobi.error
constructions.description: For implicit n≥0, A,D in R^(I×I), b,x,x₀ in R^I, and natural number k≥0, returns iterate(A,D,b,x₀,k)-x=y_k-x. The reference x is subtracted from the iterate. Its definition allows any x; the target theorem additionally assumes Ax=b.

assumptions: n is an arbitrary natural number, including 0. All matrices and vectors share the index set I=Fin n.
For the theorem, B is an arbitrary type/set and block:I→B is any function; no further condition on either is present.
For the theorem, A=D+N, D_ij=0 whenever block(i)≠block(j), and N_ij=0 whenever block(i)=block(j), for every i,j in I.
For the theorem, det D is a unit in R, equivalently det D≠0.
For the theorem, b,x are specified real vectors satisfying Ax=b.

All initial vectors x₀ and all natural iteration indices k in the error identities and bounds are universally quantified. The convergence assertion quantifies over every initial vector, with the same specified solution x.
The final sufficient convergence and Lipschitz conclusions require the additional antecedent ||-D^(-1)N||∞<1. The separate equivalence has rho(-D^(-1)N)<1 as its right-hand side.
The construction definitions require only their stated argument domains; they do not assume the theorem hypotheses.
